Definition: from G4862 and G2192; to hold together, i.e. to compress (the ears, with a crowd or siege) or arrest (a prisoner); figuratively, to compel, perplex, afflict, preoccupy:--constrain, hold, keep in, press, lie sick of, stop, be in a strait, straiten, be taken with, throng.
BiblicalUsage: Paul says the love of Christ constrains us, holding us together so that we cannot go another way, and Jesus says He has a baptism to be baptised with, and how He is straitened until it is accomplished. The same word presses from both sides: love that holds and anguish that squeezes, and both are the pressure of a purpose that must be finished.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the love of Christ constrains me more surely than any chain, and I hold that being held by His love is the freest place there is.
